title: Serum protein electrophoresis
what: This blood test sorts proteins into groups and shows how much of each there is. It helps find inflammation and unusual proteins.
why: For long-lasting inflammation, high total protein or sed rate, bone pain, kidney and liver conditions, and when a blood disorder is suspected.
duration: the blood draw usually takes 5 minutes; results usually come in a few days
tell_doctor: If you had this test before, bring the result

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually on an empty stomach: 8 to 12 hours without food. Water is fine. Check with the lab.

prepare.title: Urine
prepare.text: Sometimes a urine protein test is ordered too. Ask if you need to collect urine.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop anything on your own. Tell your doctor what you take.

bring: A urine container, if it was ordered
steps: You sit down, and a band is tied above your elbow
The skin is wiped with antiseptic
Blood is taken from a vein into a tube
The band is removed, and a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
feel: A quick prick, like a pinch
Sometimes slight dizziness. Tell the nurse, and they will help you lie down
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes
Results usually come in a few days
If an unusual protein is found, your doctor will order more tests. On its own, it is not a diagnosis

faq.q: My result says M spike. What is that?
faq.a: Too much of one type of protein was found. There are many possible causes, often harmless. Your doctor will order more tests.

faq.q: Why give a urine sample too?
faq.a: Some unusual proteins show up better in urine. The urine test adds to the blood test.

reminders.text: Serum protein electrophoresis tomorrow. Do not eat after dinner. Water is fine.
